speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Several types of family conflicts and issues go before the Courts, such as divorce, maintenance, child custody matters, family violence and youth offending.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With our rapidly greying population, we also expect to see more family disputes over mental capacity deputyship and doneeship issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In July 2014, the Committee for Family Justice recommended a number of changes to the family justice system.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The focus was on reducing acrimony in family proceedings and ensuring that the interests of children were better looked after.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Minister of State for Law, Ms Indranee Rajah, had, in her reply earlier, given a good summary of the recommendations made and the enhancements that followed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But amongst other things, the Committee recommended that a judge-led approach be taken when adjudicating family disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Their recommendations culminated in the introduction of the Family Justice Act and the establishment of the Family Justice Courts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Committee had also recommended a more robust and integrated network of community assistance and support, which led to the establishment of divorce support specialist agencies (DSSAs).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In terms of reducing the adversarial nature of family disputes, the adoption of the judge-led approach and the child-centric focus in the Family Justice Courts are significant steps in the right direction.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, the fact remains that resolution of the dispute is still being sought through the Courts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Court-based litigation is inherently adversarial, costly and potentially complex.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Research tells us that taking a "family" problem to Court can increase mistrust between the parties, reduce the likelihood of durable settlement and stoke more litigation if parental and family conflict is prolonged.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We, therefore, need to consider if there are other appropriate, multidisciplinary methods to resolve family conflict which can reduce the adversarial nature of litigation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, while mediation and counselling have been used as a core dispute resolution mechanism for some years, we want to see how it can be extended even further.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is an approach that emphasises the need to repair the harm done and restore relationships that have been damaged.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It can take place when offenders who have caused the harm reached a point when they fully, freely and genuinely admit their actions and are willing to take responsibility for them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, the core elements of restorative justice, principally the healing of relationships, reopening channels of communication, and empowering individuals to take active responsibility to repair the harm done, can potentially be applied to family conflicts as well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It can help to keep the focus on restoring family functionality through repairing family relationships.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It recognises that law is a social force that can either encourage certain behaviours or lead to certain consequences.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Therapeutic justice involves looking into whether the law can be made or applied in a more therapeutic way to relationships, so long as other values, such as justice and due process, can be fully respected.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It holds out the hope that we can foster space for family members to deliberate and explore options, while having time to manage their emotions and adjust and come to terms with new or altered personal circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Families should avail themselves of the suite of help services and not rush into commencing legal proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When families find a way to repair or reach a new equilibrium in their relationships, it should also translate into durable agreements and long-term settlements.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Importantly, children who are often the innocent victims of family conflict can benefit from a return to functioning family relationships, even if the family structure has been altered through say, a divorce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It will comprise representatives from the social services, legal practice, judiciary, academia and the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We look forward to receiving the Committee’s recommendations in due course as we work towards creating an even more holistic, restorative and therapeutic family justice ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The hon Member also asked how MSF encourages strong marriages and families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We work with community partners to offer a range of marriage support and enrichment programmes for couples at different stages of their married life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In addition, the Families for Life Council organises events, such as the annual Marriage Convention and Family 365 workshops, which cover topics, such as marriage, family life and personal life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF remains committed to promoting and funding such programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We encourage couples and families to take part in these programmes and to proactively make full use of community resources which are available to them so as to strengthen family and marital relationships all through life.
